newsitem.title: USA: Audiovox sees analysts' views as achievable.
newsitem.headline: Audiovox sees analysts' views as achievable.

text.p: Audiovox Corp said Monday it believes it can meet Wall Street earnings estimates for the rest of fiscal 1997.

"Earnings projections forecast by analysts for the balance of 1997 appear to be achievable," Audiovox Chief Executive John Shalam said in a statement released along with the company's second-quarter earnings.

The First Call consensus earnings estimate for fiscal 1997, ending in November, is $0.48 a share. Actual earnings in the first half of fiscal 1997 were $0.66 on a fully-diluted basis, and $0.22 on an operating basis.

Audiovox realized a first half gain on the sale of shares of CellStar Corp, which added about $42.1 million in cash to its balance sheet. AudioVox still owns 975,000 CellStar shares after CellStar's recent stock split.
AudioVox also said it sold 1,359,224 cellular phones in the first half of fiscal 1997 and expects to sell three million for the full fiscal year.

The company added that sales in its Automotive Electronics Division, both domestically and internationally, were up over last year, and that as a result of better margins and operating controls, profits in its domestic group also rose.
